text:
Claire (Finance): Heads up  vendor SaaSIntegrators OU invoiced with Estonian VAT (20%) on services we bought. Invoice SI-2026-11 dated 2026-04-10. We are VAT-registered in IE (IE9876543V). Should be reverse-charged B2B (no VAT charged).
SaaSIntegrators (VendorBot): Uploaded invoice SI-2026-11.pdf (net EUR 6,000; VAT EUR 1,200). Vendor VAT ID: EE123456789. Billing country: EE.
Marco (AP): Payment is scheduled tomorrow. We haven't paid yet.
Ilya (Tax): If Redwood has a valid EU VAT ID and service is B2B, place of supply is where the customer is located (Ireland) and reverse-charge applies. Vendor should not have charged Estonian VAT. We need a corrective credit note from vendor plus a new invoice stating "reverse charge" and quoting both VAT IDs and referencing Article 196 VAT Directive or local equivalent.
Claire (Finance): Ok please pause payment and ask vendor for credit note + corrected invoice. Also want vendor to explicitly state they will not remit the VAT to Estonian tax authorities for this supply.
SaaSIntegrators (VendorBot): Vendor message: "Apologies  we are registered in Estonia and had OSS configured incorrectly. We'll issue a credit note and new reverse-charge invoice by EOD"
Marco (AP): Paused payment and flagged SI-2026-11.
Claire (Finance): Suggested message to vendor (paste & send):
```
Hi <AP Contact>,

Thanks for the invoice. We are VAT registered in Ireland (IE9876543V) and this is a B2B cross-border service. Please issue: (1) a credit note cancelling SI-2026-11 (VAT EUR 1,200); (2) a replacement invoice stating net EUR 6,000, VAT 0% under reverse charge, including both VAT IDs (EE123456789 and IE9876543V), and a note: "Reverse charge applies - Article 196 VAT Directive". Please confirm you'll not remit the VAT to Estonian Tax & Customs Board for this supply.

Once we receive the credit + corrected invoice we'll resume payment.

Best,
Claire, Redwood Finance
```
Ilya (Tax): Also ask them to include a statement on the credit note referencing the original invoice number and date. We'll keep copies for EU VAT audit trail.
Ben P: Ping @EngBillingBot to add vendor flag to treat EE vendors as potentially reverse-charge when customer has EU VAT on file. Ticket for follow-up please.
EngBillingBot: Ticket TAX-548 created; assignee = Marco, due 2026-04-20.
Marco (AP): Noted. Ilya, if vendor issues corrected invoice, do we need to self-account VAT in Ireland?
Ilya (Tax): Yes, we should self-account for Irish VAT on the reverse charge (output and input VAT) in the VAT return if the service is subject. Because we can reclaim input VAT at the same time, net effect is usually zero, but it must be declared. Keep records.
SaaSIntegrators (VendorBot): Vendor uploaded credit_note_CN-2026-05.pdf and invoice SI-2026-11-RC.pdf (replacement) - notes include "reverse charge" and both VAT IDs.
Claire (Finance): Received docs. I'll attach to vendor master and update vendor tax status to "EU-B2B-REVERSE_CHARGE".
Marco (AP): Will process payment on corrected invoice tomorrow and update AP ledger with CN and replacement invoice references.
Claire (Finance): I'll log this in vendor tax exceptions and note to validate OSS settings with vendor to avoid recurrence. Closing once payment posts and records saved. :white_check_mark:
Ben P: Thanks team.
